newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends sleepy AM trade with modest gain.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends sleepy AM trade with modest gain.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures finished Thursday midsession with small gains after an uninspired, range-bound trading session.
Traders said volume was a paltry 1,155 lots with interest again centred on spread-linked dealings.
London's failure to make any major headway in either side reflected low underlying participation possibly stemmed from worries over the revised LIFFE grading terms and continued abundant supplies.
The new grading rules come into effect with the July contract. Traders said players were wary of taking delivery of May coffee in case they have to put it back on the July contract.
As such there had been a gradual liquidation of May positions and the rolling over into July and other forward months.
July finished the morning trade unchanged at $1,662 a tonne while May was $6 up at $1,639. May/July spread narrowed to $23 by the morning finish from $30 on Wednesday.

Traders said July would be well-supported by roaster and trade buying at above $1,620. But the upside potential seemed limited after July's foray into the $1,700 area earlier this week proved shortlived.
In other news, talks aimed at ending the on-going truckers' strike in Colombia remained deadlocked late on Wednesday.
The talks continued into the Wednesday night but there was no news yet on the outcome. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
